turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop thinking about my appearance. It's mostly my hairline, and just the way my face looks. I work as a host at a restaurant, and under those lights in there, I feel like I look incredibly old and... strange. 

It's pretty much taking over my thoughts. My coworkers keep telling me they don't see what I'm talking about, but I know what I see, and I just can't get it out of my head.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in their hairline and facial appearance that are not apparent to coworkers.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying that others are judging or reacting negatively to your appearance when you're interacting with them at work or elsewhere?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly noticed people reacting to me... or, you know, saying anything negative. Like I mentioned, the people I work with claim they don't even see what I'm talking about. So I don't know if the customers are judging me or not. I just... I know how bad my hairline and face look, so it's hard to imagine they aren't noticing it, but I haven't actually caught them reacting to it, if that makes sense.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses a persistent focus on perceived flaws in their hairline and face despite coworkers claiming they do not see what the patient is referring to, confirming preoccupation with perceived physical defects.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to cover up certain features, or going over conversations in your head because of how you think you look?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Especially before a shift. I... well, I keep checking the bathroom mirror over and over. I'll take pictures on my phone from different angles just to see how it looks, and I'm constantly combing my hair forward to try and cover it up. 

I also spend a lot of time just replaying in my head how the guests might be seeing me. I do all of this so much that I actually end up being late, or I just get too worked up to even go out front to the floor. It's exhausting, honestly.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors and mental acts related to appearance, including repeatedly checking the mirror, taking photos from different angles, and combing hair to camouflage features.

turns.doctor_question: When you look in the mirror or take pictures of yourself, do you feel like the reflection or image looks different from how you believe you should look, even if others don't notice anything unusual?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure if it looks different from how I *should* look... I just know it looks bad. Like, I see the hairline receding, I see the wrinkles and how old my face looks. I don't know if I have a picture in my head of how I'm supposed to look, I just know that what I see in the mirror or on my phone is... it's just awful. It doesn't matter that my coworkers say they don't see it, because I see it clear as day.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes perceiving severe flaws in physical appearance (receding hairline, wrinkles, looking old) that coworkers do not see, confirming preoccupation with perceived defects.

turns.doctor_question: How much does this concern about your appearance interfere with your ability to work, socialize, or take care of other areas of your life?
turns.patient_response:
It interferes a lot, actually. At work, I've already been written up because I end up being late or just missing shifts entirely when I get stuck in front of the mirror. It's affecting my job. 

And outside of work... I've pretty much stopped doing things. I don't go to staff photos or gallery events anymore, and I used to go hiking with people, but I've stopped that too. I just... I really can't handle being seen looking like this. It's too much.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses profound distress about their appearance and being seen by others ('I really can't handle being seen looking like this'), confirming preoccupation with appearance.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports getting 'stuck in front of the mirror' to the point of missing work shifts, demonstrating appearance-related repetitive behaviors (mirror checking).

turns.doctor_question: When you think about your hairline and the way your face looks, do you believe deep down that it’s truly defective or ugly, even though others don’t see it that way, or do you worry more about what people might think if they noticed it?
turns.patient_response: It's both, really, but... I mean, I’m here because I just can’t stop thinking about it. I honestly believe it looks terrible. Under those bright restaurant lights, I just look old and strange. I know my coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about, but I can't shake it. It's not just worrying about what they think... I genuinely see it as defective.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient explicitly confirms an inability to stop thinking about their hairline and face looking terrible and defective, despite others stating they do not see it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had the thought that if you could just fix or change the way your hairline or face looks, even slightly, it would relieve this anxiety, or does the anxiety come more from not knowing if others are reacting to it?
turns.patient_response: I don't really know if fixing it would make the anxiety go away completely. I mean... maybe? But it's hard to even imagine it being fixed. I just know that right now, looking the way I do, it causes me a lot of distress. It's not just about not knowing how others react, it's... it's just that I see it, and it looks awful to me. I haven't really thought about whether changing it slightly would help, because it just feels so overwhelmingly bad right now.
